title: 8. A Journey through States of Water

q.t: Ice, water and water vapour are…
o: Three states of the same substance
q.e: Melt ice and you get water; it is the same substance.

q.t: Which keeps its own shape?
q.e: Solids have a fixed shape.

q.t: Which takes the shape of its container but has a fixed volume?
q.e: Liquids flow but keep their volume.

q.t: Which spreads out into all available space?
q.e: Gases fill the space they're in.

q.t: Water changing into vapour is…
q.e: It happens even at room temperature.

q.t: Vapour changing into water is…
q.e: It happens when vapour touches a cold surface.

q.t: Solid changing to liquid is…
q.e: Supply heat to melt.

q.t: Liquid changing to solid is…
q.e: Cool it to freeze.

q.t: Is water vapour visible?
q.e: The visible 'steam' is tiny droplets that have already condensed.

q.t: Evaporation causes…
q.e: Evaporating water takes heat away.

q.t: Clothes dry faster on a…
q.e: Heat and wind speed up evaporation.

q.t: Clothes dry slowly on a rainy day because…
q.e: Air already holding much vapour slows evaporation.

q.t: Humidity is…
o: The amount of water vapour in the air
q.e: High humidity means slower evaporation.

q.t: Water in a flat plate dries faster than in a bottle cap because…
q.e: Bigger exposed surface → faster evaporation.

q.t: Dew on plants in the morning is caused by…
q.e: Vapour condenses on the cool leaves.

q.t: Water on a steel plate disappears but nothing seeps through. Where did it go?
q.e: It evaporated into the air.

q.t: Why does a matka keep water cool?
o: Water seeps out and evaporates, taking heat away
q.e: Its porous surface allows evaporation.

q.t: Why does sitting under a fan feel cool?
o: It lowers the room's temperature a lot
q.e: Faster evaporation means more cooling.

q.t: Why can you smell food from outside the kitchen?
o: Gases spread into all available space
q.e: The smell is in the air, which spreads.

q.t: Coconut oil solidifying in winter is…
q.e: Cooling turns the liquid to solid.

q.t: A covered glass of iced water on a balance gains mass over 30 minutes. This proves…
o: Water was gained from the air
q.e: If water seeped out, mass would stay the same; it increased, so water came from outside.

q.t: Why doesn't a stainless steel pot cool water like a matka?
q.e: No seeping, so no evaporation from its surface.

q.t: Why does sprinkling water on a roof cool it in summer?
o: The water evaporates and takes heat away
q.e: Evaporation causes cooling.

q.t: Why does hand sanitiser feel cold?
q.e: Fast evaporation = strong cooling.

q.t: An Atmospheric Water Generator makes drinking water by…
o: Cooling humid air so vapour condenses
q.e: Same effect as droplets on an iced glass.

q.t: Drops form inside a plate covering a boiling pan due to…
q.e: Vapour meets the cooler plate.

q.t: Which factor SLOWS evaporation?
q.e: Humid air already holds a lot of vapour.

q.t: Oxygen and carbon dioxide are examples of…
q.e: They have no fixed shape and spread out.

q.t: The 'steam' you see over a hot pan is…
o: Vapour partly condensed into tiny droplets
q.e: Pure vapour is invisible; droplets make it visible.

q.t: Wax, oil and ghee can also exist as…
q.e: Many substances change state with heating and cooling.

q.t: Put a cap of water in sun and one in shade. Which dries first, and why?
q.e: Heat increases evaporation.

q.t: Name the change: puddles disappearing after rain.
q.e: Water turns to vapour even without boiling.

q.t: A student says the outside of an iced glass gets wet because water seeps through. Which test proves them wrong?
o: Weighing the covered glass — mass increases
q.e: A mass increase can only come from outside.

q.t: Which change needs heat to be supplied?
q.e: Melting and evaporation take in heat.

q.t: Which change happens when vapour is cooled?
q.e: Gas → liquid on cooling.

q.t: Why are wet clothes spread out rather than kept folded to dry?
q.e: Exposed surface area matters.

q.t: Sweat drying makes you feel cooler because…
o: Evaporation takes heat from your skin
q.e: Evaporation causes cooling.

q.t: Which state has a fixed volume but no fixed shape?
q.e: A liquid fills the bottom of its container.

q.t: Is there water vapour in a dry room?
o: Yes — vapour exists at room temperature, invisibly
q.e: Vapour is always in the air around us.

q.t: Which pair are opposite changes?
q.e: Liquid → gas and gas → liquid.
